governing_principle: Verified cash from many cheap, bounded products outranks speculative startup creation, internal architecture, feature count, opportunity scores, and polished dashboards.

primary_experiment.name: Roblox micro-product factory
primary_experiment.thesis: Ship small reusable Creator Store products cheaply, measure actual buyer behavior, kill non-sellers, and concentrate engineering only where sales/reviews prove demand.
primary_experiment.initial_format: Paid models first; plugins only for genuinely tool-shaped functionality.
success_evidence: verified marketplace review or support request demonstrating use
repeat sales without additional paid acquisition
buyer request for an adjacent feature or bundle
primary_experiment.failure_rule: Do not rescue a weak SKU with more engineering. After reasonable marketplace exposure and at most one packaging/title/thumbnail iteration, a product with no buyer signal returns to HOLD or KILL while stronger SKUs receive the time.
primary_experiment.build_rule: Reuse proven generic mechanics where possible. A micro-product that exceeds the four-hour or ten-dollar cap must be split, explicitly re-approved, or stopped.
primary_experiment.rights_rule: Commercial SKUs must be original/generic implementations. Brookhaven-specific assets, proprietary UI/art, school-specific content, private data, and unverified third-party code are excluded.

resource_rules: Engineering capacity goes first to the next bounded SKU or to fixes demanded by verified buyers.
Research may inspect marketplace demand, competing listings, pricing, reviews, and buyer language but may not invent demand.
Do not build a new SaaS, marketplace, enterprise diagnostic, dashboard feature, agent hierarchy, recovery vertical, brand, or marketing site merely to create activity.
Do not use paid model/work credits above the per-SKU cap without explicit owner approval.
Actual sales and support evidence determine which product families expand.
